scenario: [LLEX.10.7.1] the lexer has no pattern-position mode: `*` is unconditionally multiplication and `.<name>` is unconditionally slot access, in every position (restated by [LLEX.17.6] and, for adapters, [LADP.3.1.1]). The shape a glob mode would read as one token is `<binding>.<slot>*<name>` with no spaces, in a pattern's `where`; here it must be a slot read times a slot read. R(a: 3, b: 4) is asserted and pumped once, and each rule reads only slots, so nothing folds at compile time and the runtime computes every product. `tight` (`r.a*r.b == 12`), `spaced` (`r.a * r.b == 12`) and `with_const` (`r.a*2 == 6`) fire, in source order. `wrong` (`r.a*r.b == 34`) does not, so the comparison is shown to be live. A lexer that took `a*r` or `a*2` as one token refuses the program or reads a different slot, and the vector goes red.
rules_ds:
schema R scope logical:
    k: Int key
    a: Int mutable
    b: Int mutable

rule tight:
    R r where r.a*r.b == 12
->
    log info "tight"

rule spaced:
    R r where r.a * r.b == 12
->
    log info "spaced"

rule with_const:
    R r where r.a*2 == 6
->
    log info "with_const"

rule wrong:
    R r where r.a*r.b == 34
->
    log info "wrong"
